correctness.rationale: For every connected triangle-free simple graph on n>=8 vertices with pairwise common-neighbor count at most two, the three-wise-connected Alexander dual has exactly edges, two-path triangles and square tetrahedra; Mantel edge counts exclude five-vertex faces. A path with unique endpoint common neighbor collapses along its private nonedge, and each four-cycle tetrahedron collapses along a private path face followed by the now-free opposite diagonal. These pairs are independent even if original square edges overlap. The residual complex is the square CW filling triangulated plus long-distance edges, each of which adds a loop. Integral Alexander duality and UCT transfer free H_2 and torsion H_1 of the square filling to degree n-5 of the ordinary cut complex and H_1 ranks plus distant loops to degree n-4. Pure shellability is obstructed if degree n-5 is nonzero. The actual embedded checker verifies all individual collapse free-face conditions and exact Smith forms in seven graph examples, including glue-two-cubes (b2=2, L=20) and a Klein grid with Z/2; finite checks corroborate but do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Full primary sections and the nearest indexed graph-wide statement were compared on mathematical implication. Bayer et al. supply two-cut triangle-free results and rectangular-grid three-cut results. The closest published-finding corpus universal edge-disjoint-square theorem is inapplicable to graphs with edge-sharing squares and cannot imply rank-two lower homology or torsion there. The new result handles all shared-edge configurations under codegree <=2 and gives a square-core homotopy equivalence, not a change of terminology. Earlier exact cube and periodic-grid classifications are special instances, not a general theorem. Unindexed broader work remains a substantive bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Search coverage does not exclude an equivalent result in unindexed square-complex, graph-ideal, Stanley-Reisner or combinatorial topology literature.
The earlier published-finding corpus edge-disjoint theorem is mathematically adjacent; the extension to shared squares is assessed by proof-level comparison, not bibliographic titles alone.

value.rationale: The object is a natural ordinary three-cut complex, and the hypotheses are an intrinsic graph codegree restriction rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The theorem reduces arbitrarily high-dimensional integral homology of all qualifying graphs to standard square-complex H_1/H_2 plus a transparent graph-distance count. This uniformly handles shared edges, detects torsion and a structural nonshellability obstruction, recovers contrasting cube/torus/Klein phenomena, and yields a nonproduct glued-cube example with two lower-degree generators. Its significance is structural homotopy reduction for a graph-wide class, not merely correct arithmetic or a minor numerical gain.
